label: Working Toolkit
notes: Open by positioning Appendix 33 as the working toolkit. Appendix 32 set up the abstract Hodge structure; this appendix sharpens the notions actually used in proofs: Lefschetz operators, primitive cohomology, polarized Hodge structures, period domains, and Griffiths transversality. The deck follows printed pages 160 through 163.

label: Lefschetz Operator
notes: Define the Lefschetz operator L as cup product with the Kahler class. On compact Kahler manifolds of complex dimension n, L raises degree by two. The hard Lefschetz theorem says that iterated L from degree n minus k to degree n plus k is an isomorphism. This is the structural rigidity that produces the diamond's reflection.

label: Primitive Cohomology
notes: Introduce primitive cohomology as the kernel of one more application of L beyond the top. Define P to the k equal to kernel of L to the (n-k+1) on H to the k. Cohomology decomposes as a sum of L-translates of primitive parts. The polarization is positive on each primitive piece up to a known sign.

label: Polarized Hodge
notes: Restate polarization in the working form. A polarized Hodge structure is a pure Hodge structure together with a bilinear form Q whose Hodge-Riemann relations are satisfied. On primitive cohomology Q is positive definite after multiplying by the standard i-to-the-power factor. The polarization makes period domains tractable.

label: Period Domain
notes: Describe period domains. Fix the Hodge numbers and the polarization type. The period domain D is the space of all polarized Hodge structures with that combinatorial data. It sits as an open subset of a flag variety, and the map from a family of varieties to D records how the Hodge filtration moves with the parameter.

label: Griffiths Transversality
notes: State Griffiths transversality. The derivative of the period map lands in F to the (p minus 1) modulo F to the p, not in arbitrary directions. This is a horizontality condition: the period map factors through a horizontal distribution on the period domain. This is the deepest constraint in the basic toolkit.

label: Working Examples
notes: Walk through working examples. Elliptic curve periods land in the upper half plane, which is the period domain for weight-one polarized structures of rank two. K3 surface periods land in a twenty-dimensional period domain. The next layer of the theory studies variations of these maps and their global properties.

label: Recap
notes: Close with the appendix recap. The basic notions for Hodge theory are: Lefschetz, primitive cohomology, polarized Hodge structures, period domains, and Griffiths transversality. Together they organize the way cohomology varies in families. This is the toolkit used throughout the main text and in Hodge-theoretic complex algebraic geometry.
